title: The course – TCS London Marathon 2026
claims: The course page describes a 26.2-mile route from Greenwich to The Mall.
There are three Start Lines.
Participants from the three starting points meet for the first time just before Mile Three in Woolwich.
The route passes through Charlton, Greenwich and Deptford and loops around Cutty Sark between Miles Six and Seven.
The route goes through Rotherhithe and Jamaica Road in Bermondsey towards Tower Bridge.
After crossing Tower Bridge, runners are north of the river and have clocked 13 miles.
The route heads east along The Highway to Westferry, then circles through Mudchute, Docklands and Canary Wharf.
Rainbow Row is a 250-metre stretch in Limehouse just past Mile 21.
The final five miles take in The Highway, Tower Hill and Victoria Embankment before Parliament Square, Birdcage Walk and the final corner in front of Buckingham Palace.
The Finish Line is on The Mall.
Toilets are available at the Start, every mile from Mile 1 to Mile 24 and at the Finish.
Accessible toilets are at the Start, the Finish, Miles 1 and 2 and every even mile until Mile 24.
BUXTON Natural Mineral Water is available every three miles from Mile 3 to 12, then every two miles from Mile 12 to 24.
Lucozade Sport is available at Miles 7, 15, 21 and 23.
Lucozade Sport Gels are available at Miles 13 and 19.
Water refill points are at Miles 5, 10, 14, 17 and 20.
The Drinks Stations are accessible for wheelchair users, and volunteers can hand drinks and open bottles.
The embedded official route on the course page shows 26.1 miles and 278 feet of elevation gain.
Official pacing advice describes wide roads and a net downhill in the first three miles, with crowding.
Official pacing advice describes Miles 4 to 14 as relatively flat with a small net negative elevation.
Official pacing advice warns of a slightly uncomfortable incline just before Tower Bridge.
Official pacing advice warns that tall buildings and narrow streets in Canary Wharf and the Westferry Underpass can cause GPS issues and wind tunnels.

Official pacing advice describes the final section from Tower Hill to Victoria Embankment as favourable for tired legs, with a right turn by Westminster Bridge about one mile to go and Birdcage Walk about one kilometre to go.
